title: Capacity playbook: dynamic commit windows & autoscale policy scenarios (Q2 roadmap)
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Goal: define a repeatable quarterly playbook that ties dynamic reservation/commit windows to concrete autoscale policy scenarios so PM, Eng, and Ops can agree on canary cadence, fallback behavior, and fiscal guardrails. Scope includes: (1) commit window templates (short, medium, long) and how to migrate customers between them; (2) autoscale policy matrix (predictive warm pools, fast-reactive surge, hedged reservations) with cost impact estimates; (3) governance rules for emergency overrides, cross-region fallbacks, and rollout phasing; (4) telemetry + dashboards required for gating decisions. This ticket captures the roadmap-level deliverables and the decision criteria we will use to convert the playbook into three ship-ready runbooks for Q2 releases.
acceptance_criteria: Three commit-window templates documented (short/14d, medium/30d, long/90d) with migration hooks and billing implications
Policy matrix published that maps workload patterns to recommended autoscale profile and expected unit-cost delta (low/medium/high)
Canary plan defined: sample size, regions, detection thresholds, rollback criteria, and success metrics (SLOs & cost targets)
Operational checklist and runbooks created for SREs to perform manual overrides and transparent customer communications
Dashboard with per-customer warm-pool occupancy, prewarm success rate, and cost-per-token projection is available in staging and referenced in the playbook
tasks: Collect 6 months of capacity consumption telemetry and build workload clusters (ENG request)
Draft commit-window templates and communicate pricing trade-offs with Finance
Define autoscale policy matrix and simulate cost/latency outcomes for 5 representative customers
Design canary gating criteria and test harness with simulated failure modes
Author runbooks, hand off to SRE for playbook validation, and schedule tabletop rehearsal
updates: 2026-02-20: Kickoff meeting with Eng, SRE, Finance. Agreed to prioritize predictive warm-pool + medium commit window for initial pilot.
2026-02-27: ENG spike (ENG-22110) completed — initial workload clusters defined; found 3 dominant patterns: bursty short-tail, steady long-tail, hybrid diurnal.
2026-03-04: Finance provided cost model for short/medium/long windows; preliminary estimates show medium window reduces tail-frequency by ~12% but increases reserved cost by ~6%.
2026-03-09: Design review with customer success. Feedback: surface per-customer rollback-friendly notifications and an opt-in telemetry export for customers on Dedicated.

2026-03-12: Decision: Canary will run in eu-west-1 and us-west-2 concurrently for 14 days with a ~5% traffic slice. ENG requested 2 additional telemetry metrics (prewarm_failure_rate, prefix_hit_ratio). Follow-up ENG tasks created.
2026-03-15: Added placeholder Grafana dashboard link and draft Confluence playbook. Next: tabletop rehearsal scheduled for 2026-04-08.
